notes: C1 adds a well-documented ParseableDiffPrefixes helper and applies it to every diff lazygit parses, including the worktree and stash diffs that previously had no override; it also generalizes prefix stripping, adds rename-to/copy-to fallbacks with proper unquoting and passes the hidden tests, but the truncated diff hides the diff --git splitting logic and any new parser tests, and the visible test changes are only mechanical argv updates.

Fixes the root cause cleanly: a shared ParseableDiffPrefixes builder forces noprefix=false and resets srcPrefix/dstPrefix while leaving mnemonicPrefix alone, and it is now also applied to the worktree and stash diffs that previously lacked it; header parsing now strips any single-component prefix, refactors unquoting, and falls back to the 'rename to'/'copy to' lines. The visible tests only update expected command args, and the truncated diff hides the diff --git splitting and any new parser tests, though the hidden tests pass.

A `keepSeries` hook on stripeSeries, backed by a new `HasExemplarAtOrAfter(lset, minValidTime)` query, keeps empty series alive in both `gc` and `gcSeries`; in `gcSeries` it also releases head and mmapped chunks, advances `firstChunkID`, clears the appender, counts chunks once, and leaves the retained series out of the min-time calculation. Two caveats: `releaseChunks` assumes the series has no OOO data but does not enforce it, and gc now takes the exemplar RLock while holding the stripe and series locks, which inverts the lock order used by the snapshot's `IterateExemplars` path (only theoretical, since the snapshot runs at shutdown). The focused tests are thorough, covering all three compaction paths, both appender APIs, zero and negative timestamps, mmapped release, idempotent re-compaction, replay-then-release, the checkpoint keeping the series record, and memory-snapshot restarts.

A `keepSeries` hook in both `stripeSeries.gc` and `gcSeries` keeps empty series that still have an exemplar at or after `minValidTime`, so their series record stays in checkpoints; `gcSeries` releases the head and mmapped chunks exactly once and the empty series does not hold back head min time. Tests are thorough and cover all three compaction paths, both appender APIs, zero/negative timestamps, the memory snapshot and replay-then-release. Two minor gaps: it assumes the newest exemplar index entry holds the maximum timestamp, and the optional-interface type assertion is slightly indirect.
